slowest_experiments.experiment: V575 terminal intake and method lock
Independent CFR row reducer, gated on Exp6592 readiness

summary: The milestone completed 6 experiments in 0.2 minutes, including 2 compute-bound entries. V575 terminal intake and method lock was the longest compute-bound entry at 0.1 minutes; the available data does not identify the cause.
bottlenecks_identified: Disk-mtime fallback timing with no live git-log commits prevents phase-level attribution; the data does not explain why the 0.1-minute compute-bound intake exceeded the 0.02-minute compute-bound reducer.
The GPU report records one Python inference process but no batch-size receipt, so the suggested batching opportunity cannot be audited from task-level evidence.
The record omits task-level model count and runner choice. DualGPURunner applicability is therefore undetermined.
improvements_suggested: Batch 8-16 questions per forward pass and record the effective batch size; the GPU monitor projects a 4-8x throughput improvement.
Emit per-task phase timing, GPU utilization, model count, batch size, and runner-selection receipts instead of relying only on disk-mtime reconstruction.
Use model-count-aware scheduling: keep a single GGUF model on one GPU, and dispatch across both GPUs only when 2 or more models run concurrently.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add 8-16-question inference batching with measured batch-size and throughput receipts.
Capture task-scoped phase and GPU telemetry for every compute-bound experiment.
Record model count and runner choice, then route concurrent multi-model work across both GPUs.
meta_reflection: The locked GPU-idle field is false, and the active GPU reached 97% utilization, so the retrospective does not classify GPU idle as a compute-bound bottleneck. The 45% estimate applies the lower 4x batching projection to the 0.12 compute-bound minutes within 0.2 total minutes; it is conditional because the data does not identify the batchable share.
